page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.medium is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a single-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor operating at a dedicated frequency of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 6.0 GB of system memory. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 937 GB NVMe SSD. It also provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show average single-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1499.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 940.0. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks are poor, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 938.0. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, measuring 59.32 GB/sec for small cached reads and dropping to 19.51 GB/sec for large uncached reads. Database operations on Redis reach 1.21 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput is recorded at 1.13 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the is4gen.medium offers high local NVMe storage density relative to its single-vCPU compute footprint. This makes it a practical choice for storage-heavy workloads that do not demand high CPU or memory performance. The primary tradeoff is the limited processing power and memory bandwidth. This instance is best suited for lightweight databases, local caching, log indexing, and basic file-serving applications.
